headline: CISA confirmed active exploitation of critical Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud flaws, researchers traced the Node.js remote code execution bug to a Brotli decoder defect now found in Bun, Python, and Envoy, and LiteLLM pinned its poisoned release on a master key a developer committed to a public GitHub repository in May.

emerging_trends.text: AI tooling now works both ends of a disclosure, surfacing the years-old PHP2Shell bugs for researchers in August 2026 and then helping attackers assemble working exploits within days of the October patches.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Hands Attackers the PHP2Shell Bugs

emerging_trends.text: A single memory-corruption bug in Google's Brotli decoder has surfaced in Node.js, Bun, Python packages, and Envoy proxies, proof that one bundled compression library carries its flaws into every runtime that ships it.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Reaches Bun, Python, and Envoy

emerging_trends.text: Credentials left in public repositories keep becoming supply chain compromises, as LiteLLM found when it traced its backdoored 1.107.0 release to an Agent Platform master key a developer committed to GitHub five months earlier.
emerging_trends.topic_title: A Public Repository Master Key Opened LiteLLM

topics.title: AI Hands Attackers the PHP2Shell Bugs
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported on October 24, 2026 that security researchers used AI tools to dig the years-old flaws out of the PHP scripting language in the first place, and that AI-assisted exploitation attempts followed the patches, while Dark Reading walked administrators through assessing exposure because the fix takes more than clicking update.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, the pair the industry calls PHP2Shell, reach web servers and content management systems worldwide, and the PHP Foundation shipped fixes in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Identify every PHP interpreter in the estate, including those embedded in vendor appliances that carry no fixed release yet, and apply the mitigation PHP published for the separate unpatched flaw CVE-2026-115560.

sources.title: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable
Exposed to PHP2Shell? Cyber Experts Weigh in With Advice
PHP Vulnerability Wrap-Up, (Fri, Oct 23rd)

topics.title: A Public Repository Master Key Opened LiteLLM
topics.latest_developments: LiteLLM disclosed on Friday, October 23, 2026 that a configuration file committed to the public LiteLLM-Labs/lite-harness repository on May 27, 2026 carried the master key to an Agent Platform deployment, which the attacker used to steal GitHub tokens and seize the release pipeline, and Microsoft Threat Intelligence published its own breakdown of the malicious 1.107.0 package the same day.
topics.summary: LiteLLM is the Python package that routes applications to large language models; version 1.107.0, published to PyPI and Docker Hub on October 21, 2026, used Python startup hooks to steal cloud logins, developer secrets, and AI service API keys and to load further code remotely. PyPI has quarantined the release, and anyone who installed it should rotate every credential the host touched.

sources.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks

topics.title: Eye Security Switched Off Two Million Popcorn Time Updaters
topics.latest_developments: The Dutch security firm Eye Security disclosed that between November 2025 and March 2026 it pushed more than 2 million updates to computers it does not own, disabling the background updater inside Time4Popcorn, an abandoned fork of the Popcorn Time BitTorrent streaming app.
topics.summary: The abandoned updater let anyone who controlled its channel run code with elevated privileges on millions of Windows machines, and no maintainer remained to fix it. Eye Security's remote shutdown closed the hole and raises the question of who may legally patch software on strangers' computers.

sources.title: Researchers Push Over 2 Million Updates to Remotely Disable Popcorn Time Updater That Could Fuel a Botnet
Abandoned Popcorn Time app exposed millions of devices to RCE attacks

topics.title: CISA Adds Collabora and VeloCloud to KEV
topics.latest_developments: CISA added two critical flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Friday, October 23, 2026, citing active exploitation: CVE-2026-110447, an operating system command injection bug rated 9.2 in the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server, and the SQL injection flaw in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator that Arista Networks patched on October 22, 2026.
topics.summary: Collabora Online's built-in CODE Server renders documents inside Nextcloud and similar platforms, and VeloCloud Orchestrator runs VeloCloud SD-WAN networks; the VeloCloud bug lifts a read-only customer login to operator privileges. Federal agencies face a KEV remediation deadline, and every other operator of either product should patch immediately and hunt for prior access.

sources.title: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Critical Flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud

topics.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Reaches Bun, Python, and Envoy
topics.latest_developments: Researchers established that CVE-2026-111497, the memory-corruption bug behind this week's Node.js remote code execution, sits in Google's Brotli decoder itself and therefore in Bun, the Python brotli and brotlicffi packages, and Envoy proxies configured to decompress Brotli.
topics.summary: Crafted Brotli-compressed data overwrites memory past the end of a buffer, and any service that unpacks attacker-supplied Brotli streams inherits the flaw. Inventory every runtime, package, and proxy that decodes Brotli rather than treating the Node.js 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x updates as the end of the work.

sources.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Behind Node.js RCE Also Affects Bun, Python and Other Widely Used Software

topics.title: Britain Weighs 14 Years for Cable Sabotage
topics.latest_developments: The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport published a White Paper this week proposing 14-year prison terms for deliberately damaging undersea cables and pipelines off the British coast, plus unlimited fines for ship owners whose vessels cause the damage.
topics.summary: The plan would replace the Submarine Telegraph Act 1885, which caps punishment at a 1,000-pound fine and five years in prison, a penalty the government considers useless against state-linked hybrid operations that drag anchors through subsea infrastructure. Telecommunications and energy operators with British landing stations should expect new reporting and protection duties to accompany the sentencing changes.

sources.title: UK proposes 14-year prison terms for undersea cable sabotage
UK proposes 14-year jail terms for subsea cable saboteurs

business_politics.title: France Puts 70,000 Officers on the Streets
business_politics.latest_developments: The French government deployed 70,000 police officers Saturday, October 24, a 20% increase over last weekend, as the Yellow Vest movement rejoined the demonstrations and the yields on some French corporate bonds fell below the yield on French government debt.
business_politics.summary: Mass protests over living costs turned into riots and looting across Paris, Marseille, and other French cities last weekend, and the new round of marches tests President Emmanuel Macron, whom critics on both the left and the right blame for the disorder. The Financial Times describes a country running short of money, patience, and answers six months before the presidential election, with Marine Le Pen waiting in the wings.

sources.title: France deploys 70,000 officers to police latest protests
France Girds for Another Day of Protest After Widespread Violence
The Yellow Vests Are Back on the Streets of France in Test for Government
French government and corporate bond yields are converging
France is looking ungovernable. And it's going to get worse

business_politics.title: Memo Says Iranian Plots Against Americans Reach Advanced Stages
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported early Saturday, October 24, that a United States intelligence memo puts Iranian plans to kill American citizens in the Middle East at advanced stages, and the Wall Street Journal filmed sailors aboard the USS George Washington rearming the strike group for possible strikes on Iran.
business_politics.summary: The United States Navy blockade and air sanctions have tightened around Tehran, and Pakistan and Iraq have closed some border crossings that carried the overland trade cushioning Iran's economy. Renewed American strikes would put Gulf energy exports, shipping, and the region's remaining diplomacy at risk.

sources.title: Intelligence memo warns Iran plotting to kill Americans in Middle East
Aboard USS George Washington as It Rearms for Possible Iran Strikes
Iran Is Now Losing Overland Trade Routes to U.S. Pressure

business_politics.title: Ukraine Says Starlink Runs Normally Again
business_politics.latest_developments: Ukraine's military said Saturday, October 24, that Elon Musk's SpaceX has lifted the Starlink speed restrictions that had hampered its drone forces since October 14, reversing the throttling Kyiv complained about through Friday.
business_politics.summary: The caps degraded the Starlink links Ukraine's drone units use to strike Russian targets and intercept incoming drones, and Kyiv had accused Washington of slowing the service deliberately after President Trump telephoned Musk about it. Russia has kept up missile and drone barrages on Kyiv and the Ukrainian power grid through the dispute.

sources.title: Ukraine military says Starlink service restrictions have been removed
Ukraine's Military Starlink Is Working Again, Kyiv Says

business_politics.title: JetBlue Creditors Hire Restructuring Advisers
business_politics.latest_developments: Senior creditors to JetBlue Airways have retained the financial adviser PJT Partners and the law firm Akin as the airline's shares and bonds sink, the Wall Street Journal reported Saturday, October 24.
business_politics.summary: Lenders organize advisers of that sort when they expect to negotiate over a borrower's debt. JetBlue's bonds and equity have both fallen, putting one of the larger United States carriers and its aircraft and card-partner financing in front of bank credit committees.

sources.title: JetBlue Creditors Hire Advisers as Airline's Shares, Bonds Sink

business.title: Oakford Park Fruit Market Comes Back
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Saturday, October 24, that Greg Forejt Jr., who owns Windy Heights Farm in East Huntingdon, will revive the Oakford Park Fruit Market near Jeannette.
business.summary: The roadside market sold fresh produce for decades and closed last year when its owner retired. Forejt will run it alongside his East Huntingdon farm, returning a produce outlet to the Jeannette area in Westmoreland County.

sources.title: Owner of Windy Heights Farm in East Huntingdon to revive Oakford Park Fruit Market near Jeannette

business.title: Row House Hollywood Bets on Dormont
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Saturday, October 24, that Row House Hollywood, the movie theater in Dormont, is drawing on the building's history as it works out a future as a community theater.
business.summary: The Hollywood Theater sits on Potomac Avenue in the Dormont business district, one of the few single-screen neighborhood houses left in Allegheny County, and Row House now programs it. Its model tests whether a small borough can support a theater against streaming and the multiplexes.

sources.title: Row House Hollywood in Dormont looks to the past for a community movie theater's future

around_town.title: Shapiro Signs the Meeting Notice Fix
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported Saturday, October 24, that Governor Josh Shapiro signed legislation Thursday, October 22, closing a loophole in Pennsylvania's open meetings law.
around_town.summary: The law clarifies and claws back exceptions to the 24-hour rule that requires public bodies in Pennsylvania to publish voting agendas before they meet, a rule boroughs, townships, and school boards had used the exceptions to sidestep. Residents who follow local government now get earlier notice of what their elected officials will vote on.

sources.title: Lawmakers send Shapiro bill to close meeting notice loophole in Pa. transparency law

around_town.title: University Line Paving Starts Monday in Oakland and Uptown
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Regional Transit announced its paving plan Friday, October 23, with the next step of Phase 2 of the University Line starting Monday, October 26, in Oakland and Uptown.
around_town.summary: The nearly $300 million University Line will run bus rapid transit between downtown Pittsburgh and Oakland, and the construction has moved through Uptown and Oakland streets in stages. Drivers, bus riders, and businesses along the route face another round of lane and street work.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Regional Transit announces latest plans for paving in Oakland, Uptown

around_town.title: NFL House Closes in Paris as Trump Second-Guesses the Game
around_town.latest_developments: The NFL shut its NFL House fan venue in Paris on Saturday, October 24, ahead of the day's street protests, and President Trump said the league "could have probably postponed" Sunday's Steelers-Saints game over the unrest.
around_town.summary: Commissioner Roger Goodell said the league planned the Paris trip in consultation with United States and French authorities and called street protests "not unusual in France." The game kicks off Sunday, October 25, at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on NFL Network, with thousands of Pittsburgh fans in the city.

sources.title: NFL House in Paris closes ahead of street protests in French capital
Trump expresses concern about NFL game and civil unrest in Paris

events.title: ScareHouse Founder Opens a North Shore Haunt
events.latest_developments: TribLive reported Saturday, October 24, that Scott Simmons, who founded ScareHouse 25 years ago, has brought a new kind of Halloween attraction to Pittsburgh's North Shore.
events.summary: Simmons built ScareHouse in Etna into one of the country's better-known haunted houses, and his new North Shore show reaches for effects he has not used before, tentacles among them. The attraction runs through the Halloween season.

sources.title: ScareHouse founder brings new kind of Halloween experience to Pittsburgh's North Shore

events.title: Night of the Singing Dead Returns to City Winery
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Saturday, October 24, that Night of the Singing Dead comes back to Pittsburgh City Winery for a final edition.
events.summary: The Halloween-season music show has run as a Pittsburgh tradition and plays City Winery on Smallman Street in the Strip District. The Post-Gazette casts this run as the last one.

sources.title: Night of the Singing Dead comes back to life — for one last laugh

around_teams.title: The NFL's International Endgame
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published a piece Saturday, October 24, asking where the NFL's overseas expansion leads as the Steelers prepare to play the league's first game in Paris.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh meets the New Orleans Saints Sunday, October 25, at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on NFL Network, the league's debut in France. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers has said the NFL could stage 16 international games in a single week and that he would support it, and the Post-Gazette weighs that ambition against the travel burden on players and the league's hunt for new audiences.

sources.title: As the Steelers play the first game in Paris, what is the NFL's international endgame here?
Aaron Rodgers says the NFL could play 16 international games in one week — and he'd support it

around_teams.title: Holmes and Shazier Work Paris for the Team Channel
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers' channel posted Santonio Holmes and Ryan Shazier live from Paris on Friday, October 23, along with shorts of players testing their French.
around_teams.summary: Holmes, the Super Bowl XLIII most valuable player, and Shazier, the former inside linebacker, join Hall of Famers Dermontti Dawson and Mel Blount among the alumni the team has sent to France for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints. The channel has filled the week with street videos from Paris alongside its Friday media sessions.

sources.title: Santonio Holmes & Ryan Shazier live from Paris 🙌🇫🇷
Pittsburgh meets Paris 🤝🇫🇷

team_usa.title: NWSL Drops the Rodman Rule Restrictions
team_usa.latest_developments: The National Women's Soccer League and its players association agreed to strip the qualifying restrictions out of the High Impact Player rule, ESPN reported, making every player in the league eligible.
team_usa.summary: The rule, known around the league as the Rodman rule, let clubs pay certain stars outside the salary budget and limited which players could qualify. Removing the restrictions widens the pool of players, United States national team regulars among them, whose clubs can pay them through the exception.

sources.title: NWSL dropping 'Rodman rule' restrictions; all players eligible
